newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy economy needs lower interest rates now - Dini.
newsitem.headline: Italy economy needs lower interest rates now - Dini.

text.p: Foreign minister and former prime minister Lamberto Dini said the Italian economy was in need of lower interest rates and this was the right moment.
"Today our economy absolutely needs" a reduction of interest rates and "now is the moment", Dini, a former central banker, told a meeting here.
Dini, speaking at a meeting with the media here, said Italian inflation, which grew at 2.6 percent year on year in November, had made much progress.

"When compared with bank rates these are extremely high. There is a lot to do both to improve the efficiency of the banks, which isn't a short term matter, and to bring about a reduction in rates," he said.

Dini also said he hoped an eventual European Union stability pact to enforce fiscal discipline after monetary union would be a balanced pact which everyone could live with, saying it needed to be "reasonable and not deflationary".
EU monetary officials and finance ministers are holding meetings over today and Thursday to iron out differences on the pact before an EU leaders' summit in Dublin on Friday.
